layers.name: Energy
layers.description: More generation and a stronger grid are foundations for industrial growth. Track dependable power for AI factories and communities, alongside storage, efficiency and affordability.
layers.connection: Delivered electricity supports chip fabrication and AI factories. New power and grid projects can also create work for local builders and equipment suppliers; realized benefits need local evidence.
focus: New generation, firm power and commissioning
Local jobs, supplier spending and electricity affordability
layers.outlook: Track new generation, grid delivery and demand together. More annual energy does not automatically provide power in the right place at the right time.

layers.name: Chips
layers.description: Compute, memory, storage and networking chips make the AI factory possible. Design, fabrication, advanced packaging and manufacturing equipment turn ideas into working silicon.
layers.connection: Accelerators need memory, storage and network connectivity. Domestic fabs and suppliers connect this layer to industrial capacity, while deployed systems connect it to useful compute.
focus: Chip designers, fabs and manufacturing equipment
Accelerators, memory, storage and advanced packaging
Networking silicon, optical connections and delivered supply
layers.outlook: Follow operational fabs and reproducible system benchmarks. Process-node names alone do not establish speed, efficiency or available AI capacity.

layers.name: Infrastructure
layers.description: AI factories bring power, chips, storage, networking and cooling together. They provide the compute for models to produce useful intelligence, generated reasoning and actions.
layers.connection: Scale up within systems, scale out across clusters, and scale across sites. Copper and optical connections help turn individual chips into capacity for training and inference.
focus: Operational capacity, grid delivery and commissioning
Local purchasing, construction work and operating jobs
layers.outlook: Follow projects from announcement through financing, construction and operation. Site counts and investment pledges are context, not delivered compute.

layers.name: Models
layers.description: Model companies and open communities build LLMs and other models. Harnesses connect them to context and tools; agent systems organize their capabilities into useful work.
layers.connection: AI factories supply compute. Models, harnesses and agent systems connect that compute to digital workers, robotics and scientific applications; reliability determines practical value.
focus: Model and agent reliability on completed tasks
Harnesses, tool use and human intervention
Inference cost, efficiency, openness and scientific capability
layers.outlook: Track capability, reliability, cost and openness separately. Better benchmark scores need to translate into dependable performance in real tasks.

layers.name: Applications
layers.description: Put intelligence to work: digital workers for companies, productive robots in the physical world, and advances in medicine, engineering, climate research and clean energy. Track demonstrated outcomes.
layers.connection: Applications turn model capability into business value and physical or scientific results. Useful demand can support the layers below; adoption alone does not establish economic benefit.
focus: Digital workers: completed work, quality and business value
Industrial, mobile and humanoid robot deployments
Healthcare, drug discovery, engineering, climate and clean energy
layers.outlook: Follow useful work from trials into sustained deployment. Measure productivity, robot reliability and validated scientific or patient outcomes; keep future ambitions distinct from demonstrated results.

metrics.title: Global data-center electricity demand
metrics.scope: All data centers, including non-AI workloads. Annual electricity consumption; not generation capacity.
metrics.note: 2024 is the 2025 report baseline; 2025 and 2030 use the updated 2026 IEA outlook. The 2030 value is a forecast, not a generation target.

metrics.title: U.S. data-center electricity demand
metrics.scope: All U.S. data centers. 2028 is a modeled range from the 2024 report, retained as a historical forecast vintage.
metrics.note: The 2028 interval is 325–580 TWh. A newer LBNL update exists; this series remains explicitly dated until reviewed.

metrics.title: U.S. nuclear capacity ambition
metrics.scope: Total U.S. nuclear generating capacity across the economy; not allocated to AI.
metrics.note: DOE describes an approximately 100 GW starting fleet and a 400 GW goal for 2050. The starting point is not a current progress measurement.

metrics.title: TSMC annual manufacturing capacity
metrics.scope: All TSMC-managed facilities and subsidiaries; includes non-AI chips and mature processes.
metrics.note: Company-reported capacity exceeds 17 million wafers in 2025. This measures manufacturing context, not AI accelerator shipments.

metrics.title: U.S. data-center footprint
metrics.scope: Stanford AI Index 2026 reported count of U.S. data centers; all types, not AI-only facilities.
metrics.note: A site count describes geographic footprint. It does not measure operational MW, utilization or installed AI compute. Period is the report vintage (2026).

metrics.title: Microsoft Wisconsin investment commitments
metrics.scope: Wisconsin data-center investment pledges; initial facility and additional second facility. Not recognized expenditure.
metrics.note: The September 2025 announcement adds $4B over three years to the initial $3.3B pledge. Completion and actual expenditure require subsequent evidence.

metrics.title: The falling cost of useful intelligence
metrics.scope: Cost of querying a model at GPT-3.5-equivalent MMLU performance, as defined by Stanford AI Index 2025.
metrics.note: Two historical price observations at a comparable benchmark threshold. These are not current provider prices or a universal capability measure.

metrics.title: AI use is becoming part of everyday work
metrics.scope: Organizations reporting AI use in at least one business function, as summarized by Stanford AI Index from survey evidence. Not population-wide adoption.
metrics.note: Survey-based adoption across annual report vintages; sampling and methodology may change. Adoption is distinct from measured productivity or return on investment.

metrics.title: NextEra Energy · annual revenue
metrics.scope: Company-wide operating revenue, including FPL and NextEra Energy Resources.
metrics.note: Broader power business; this is not revenue from AI customers alone. Preliminary results release.

metrics.title: GE Vernova · annual revenue
metrics.scope: Company-wide GAAP revenue across Power, Wind and Electrification.
metrics.note: Equipment revenue includes many uses beyond AI and data centers.

metrics.title: Schneider Electric · annual revenue
metrics.scope: Company-wide revenue across Energy Management and Industrial Automation.
metrics.note: Not an AI revenue breakout. Original euros are retained; no exchange-rate conversion.

metrics.title: NVIDIA · annual revenue
metrics.scope: Company-wide annual revenue.
metrics.note: Includes Data Center, gaming and other markets; not a measure of AI-only sales. NVIDIA designs chips and relies on manufacturing partners.

metrics.title: AMD · annual revenue
metrics.scope: Company-wide annual revenue.
metrics.note: Data Center segment revenue was $16.6B in FY2025; that includes server CPUs as well as AI accelerators.

metrics.title: Broadcom · annual revenue
metrics.scope: Company-wide annual net revenue, semiconductors plus infrastructure software.
metrics.note: Includes VMware and other non-AI businesses. Custom chip design is distinct from wafer fabrication.

metrics.title: TSMC · annual revenue
metrics.scope: Company-wide annual revenue, using TSMC’s reported U.S. dollar figure.
metrics.note: All customers and chip markets; not AI-only. Annual wafer capacity is tracked separately.

metrics.title: Samsung Electronics · annual revenue
metrics.scope: Company-wide annual revenue in trillions of Korean won.
metrics.note: Includes phones, displays and appliances. This figure is not semiconductor, foundry or AI revenue.

metrics.title: Intel · annual revenue
metrics.scope: Consolidated company-wide annual revenue.
metrics.note: Internal foundry transfers are not additional consolidated sales; do not add segment revenues without eliminations.

metrics.title: SK hynix · annual revenue
metrics.scope: Company-wide annual revenue in trillions of Korean won.
metrics.note: Total memory business; not an HBM-only or AI-only revenue figure.

metrics.title: Micron · annual revenue
metrics.scope: Company-wide annual revenue.
metrics.note: Includes memory and storage outside AI. This is fiscal 2025, not a 2026 run rate.

metrics.title: ASML · annual revenue
metrics.scope: Company-wide annual net sales.
metrics.note: ASML sells manufacturing equipment; it does not fabricate customers’ finished chips. Original euros retained.

metrics.title: Vertiv · annual revenue
metrics.scope: Company-wide annual net sales.
metrics.note: Critical digital infrastructure sales, not solely AI data centers.

metrics.title: Microsoft · annual revenue
metrics.scope: Company-wide annual revenue.
metrics.note: Azure exceeded $100B annual revenue in FY2026, but Azure includes non-AI workloads. Copilot is not the whole company.

metrics.title: Amazon Web Services · annual revenue
metrics.scope: AWS segment annual net sales; excludes Amazon retail and other segments.
metrics.note: A segment figure, not total Amazon revenue. Includes non-AI cloud services; not AI-only sales.

metrics.title: Alphabet / Google · annual revenue
metrics.scope: Consolidated Alphabet annual revenue.
metrics.note: Includes advertising and other businesses; not Google Cloud or Gemini revenue alone.

metrics.title: Meta · annual revenue
metrics.scope: Company-wide annual revenue.
metrics.note: Predominantly the broader advertising business; not standalone model revenue or a direct measure of AI value added.

metrics.title: OpenAI · annualized revenue run rate
metrics.scope: Company-reported annualized revenue run rate; not revenue earned over a full year.
metrics.note: Historical run-rate disclosure. It is not an audited annual revenue total or a current September 2026 estimate.

metrics.title: Anthropic · annualized revenue run rate
metrics.scope: Company-reported annualized revenue run rate; not revenue earned over a full year.
metrics.note: Historical company disclosure from May 2026. Funding raised and valuation are separate from revenue.

metrics.title: Salesforce · annual revenue
metrics.scope: Company-wide annual revenue.
metrics.note: Includes the wider CRM and data business; not Agentforce-only revenue or measured customer productivity.

metrics.title: Palantir · annual revenue
metrics.scope: Company-wide annual revenue, rounded as described in the annual report.
metrics.note: Government and commercial platform revenue; not AIP-only sales or a quantified economy-wide productivity effect.

metrics.title: Global advanced logic capacity · 7nm and below
metrics.scope: Global 300mm fabrication capacity at 7nm and below, across all chip uses.
metrics.note: June 2025 forecast vintage. Later calendar years remain forecasts until an observed update is sourced. Wafer capacity is not accelerator shipments.

metrics.title: Global 300mm memory capacity
metrics.scope: Global 300mm memory fabrication capacity, including DRAM and NAND.
metrics.note: June 2026 forecast vintage. This is not HBM-only capacity and cannot be translated directly into GPU supply.

metrics.title: U.S. utility-scale solar additions
metrics.scope: New utility-scale solar nameplate capacity; not annual generation or dependable capacity.
metrics.note: EIA February 2026 inventory: reported 2025 additions versus developers’ 2026 plans. Plans are not delivered capacity.

metrics.title: U.S. utility-scale battery additions
metrics.scope: New battery discharge-power capacity; not energy generated or stored energy in GWh.
metrics.note: EIA February 2026 inventory: reported 2025 additions versus developers’ 2026 plans. Plans are not delivered capacity.

metrics.title: Generation and storage in U.S. interconnection queues
metrics.scope: Active proposed generation and storage capacity at end-2025; queue coverage spans approximately 98% of installed U.S. generation.
metrics.note: Queue entry is a development signal, not financing, an interconnection agreement or operational supply.

metrics.title: Gemini solar generating capacity
metrics.scope: Company-reported solar power capacity at commercial operation; variable output.
metrics.note: Project-specific disclosure. Preserve source date, stage and scope; do not aggregate unlike capacity measures.

metrics.title: Gemini battery power capacity
metrics.scope: Battery discharge-power capacity, separate from solar generation.
metrics.note: Project-specific disclosure. Preserve source date, stage and scope; do not aggregate unlike capacity measures.

metrics.title: Gemini battery energy capacity
metrics.scope: Company-reported stored-energy capacity. Do not derive it from nominal discharge power and duration.
metrics.note: Project-specific disclosure. Preserve source date, stage and scope; do not aggregate unlike capacity measures.

metrics.title: CHPE transmission transfer capacity
metrics.scope: Transmission capability at commercial operation, not new generation capacity or observed continuous flow.
metrics.note: Project-specific disclosure. Preserve source date, stage and scope; do not aggregate unlike capacity measures.

metrics.title: Cape Station Phase I planned capacity
metrics.scope: Planned total across three GeoBlocks. First power on one block does not commission the whole phase.
metrics.note: Project-specific disclosure. Preserve source date, stage and scope; do not aggregate unlike capacity measures.

metrics.title: Cape Station Phase II planned capacity
metrics.scope: Eight planned GeoBlocks in the second phase, distinct from Phase I.
metrics.note: Project-specific disclosure. Preserve source date, stage and scope; do not aggregate unlike capacity measures.

metrics.title: Crane restart planned capacity
metrics.scope: Capacity proposed for restart in the September 2024 announcement. Updated timing is tracked separately.
metrics.note: Project-specific disclosure. Preserve source date, stage and scope; do not aggregate unlike capacity measures.

metrics.title: Project Rainier deployed Trainium2 chips
metrics.scope: Trainium2 chip count in the operating Rainier cluster. Not MW, GPU-equivalent compute or global accelerator supply.
metrics.note: Project-specific disclosure. Preserve source date, stage and scope; do not aggregate unlike capacity measures.

metrics.title: AWS Trainium2 chips landed
metrics.scope: Company-reported chips landed across the fleet. Includes Rainier; not equivalent to all chips operating simultaneously.
metrics.note: Project-specific disclosure. Preserve source date, stage and scope; do not aggregate unlike capacity measures.

metrics.title: Abilene original eight-building campus plan
metrics.scope: Planned campus power capacity, not confirmed commissioned IT load. Excludes separately announced later campus expansions.
metrics.note: Project-specific disclosure. Preserve source date, stage and scope; do not aggregate unlike capacity measures.

metrics.title: Meta Richland Parish campus plan
metrics.scope: Issuer-described compute capacity in a campus expansion plan. Electrical versus IT-load accounting is not clarified in this disclosure.
metrics.note: Project-specific disclosure. Preserve source date, stage and scope; do not aggregate unlike capacity measures.

metrics.title: U.S. electricity generation growth · first half
metrics.unit: billion kWh versus prior-year first half
metrics.scope: Change in electric power sector generation in 1H2026 compared with 1H2025. Not total generation, capacity or electricity dedicated to AI.
metrics.note: EIA August 2026 reports a 37 billion kWh increase, or 1.8%, in first-half generation. This historical estimate is subject to revision.

targets.title: Plan for global data-center electricity demand
targets.detail: Demand projection for all data centers. A matched generation-and-grid delivery series is needed to assess readiness.

targets.title: Expand U.S. nuclear generating capacity
targets.detail: Economy-wide target. The approximate starting fleet is not a current measurement of additions toward the goal.

targets.title: Build a second Wisconsin data center
targets.detail: Three-year spending pledge. We need subsequent expenditure and commissioning evidence before assessing delivery.
